$schemaNote: Escape hatch for scripts/reachability.mjs (Phase 6.2). Each entry names a symbol + its declaring file that the gate found unreachable and that the team has knowingly deferred. An entry requires a reason, a gap/ADR reference, and an expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD). An expired entry FAILS the gate — substrate is a dated, self-cancelling exception, not a silent norm. Entries tagged with an existing G-xx id match the Verified gap register in ROADMAP.md. Expiry is tiered, not blanket, per the 2026-08-04 remediation pass (this repo ships waves on a roughly one-day cadence, so a uniform 6-week grace was never proportionate to actual velocity): G-14 entries (capability.ts/capability-token.ts) are tied to ADR-028, the record that decides whether to wire or delete them; pre-existing registered-gap entries (G-01, G-02, G-04, G-06, G-11, G-12, G-29, G-32) expire in 21 days (established architectural gaps whose closure plausibly spans more than one wave). The 2026-08-04 first sweep (94 previously-uncatalogued dead exports found when the 6.2 gate first ran) was retriaged wave1/gate-honesty (2026-08-04, same day): folded into an existing gap row where one genuinely fit (G-29, G-32, above); tagged DEFERRED-WAVE1-LOOP-AS-JOB-2026-08-04 / DEFERRED-WAVE1-TUI-CONTRACTS-2026-08-04 (10-day expiry, 2026-08-14) where an active same-wave lane's stated scope plausibly reaches the symbol and re-triage after that lane lands is the right next step; tagged RECOMMEND-DELETION-2026-08-04 (14-day expiry, 2026-08-18) where no active lane's scope plausibly reaches the symbol and the honest recommendation is deletion or a deliberate ADR + gap-register row, not indefinite deferral. None of these three new tags are Verified-gap-register G-xx ids — they are dated, reasoned placeholders pending that decision, consistent with this file's existing NEW-6.2-2026-08-04 convention.

CORRECTED 2026-08-27 per ADR-138 (accepted the same day): the sentence above describing this as a boundary around retrieval 'introduced by ADR-112' overstates what runs. The offline boundary is unchanged and still correct; only its description was wrong.

The one-catalog-reader consolidation (todo 9) moved the runtime-catalog parse out of three divergent readers into this module, and gate:package-boundaries now forbids a packages/ file importing scripts/ in-process, so the two .mjs consumers reach it through the package's public index re-export. This gate's analysis is static and does not follow a re-export barrel, so both symbols read as unreachable while registration-integrity.mjs and catalog-parser.mjs genuinely call them. The alternative is a call site invented only to satisfy the gate, which would make the graph claim a consumption path that does not exist. AUTHORED 2026-09-30.
